stem.en: Kabir asks why a single glowing bacterium "does not just glow anyway, to be helpful". What does a lone glow cost?

text.en: Coins, for a light no one can see. One cell's glow is invisible; only a million together light the squid. A cell that glows alone spends for nothing, and a cell that waits for the quorum spends only when the light will count.

feedback.en: The glow enzyme burns fuel and coins. It is one of the most expensive things a bacterium does.
One cell's light is far too faint to affect anything, which is the point.

text.en: It would be seen by fish.

feedback.en: The squid wants to be seen, as moonlight. The lone cell's problem is waste, not danger.

explanation.en: Some jobs only pay when done together. Quorum sensing lets each cell wait until enough others will join in.
